segments.text: The Scorch lived up to its name at dawn.
Heat shimmered off the dunes like liquid gold, warping the horizon into a wavering mirage.
Sweat evaporated before it could bead, stolen by the parched air.
Legionnaires shuffled forward, cloaks pulled high against the glare, boots sinking ankle-deep in scalding sand.
Pack-lizards snorted plumes of steam, their scaled hides darkened by dust.
Even Zaron’s hum within Geralt’s armor felt muffled, dampened by the oppressive stillness.
Only Oreck moved with unbroken vigilance, his chroniton-flecked gaze scanning the blinding expanse.
He felt it first – a low-frequency tremor transmitted through the sand, a vibration felt more than heard, prickling the skin beneath his scales.
Midway down the strung-out column, Private Ren stumbled.
"Stars… my ears… ringing…" Beside him, Corporal Vess frowned.
Too silent—" Her words cut off as the ground erupted *behind* them.
Fountains of superheated sand geysered skyward, revealing three monstrous silhouettes clawing free.
Towering slabs of distorted muscle and scarred hide, their useless wings pinned tight against bulging backs.
Their faces were grotesque masks of reptilian fury, eyes burning with agonized madness.
One threw back its head, jaws distending impossibly wide.
The air itself seemed to *congeal*, then shatter.
A focused beam of pure sonic torment ripped forward—not sound, but a physical wave of concussive disintegration.
It struck the rearmost pack-lizard and its guard detail.
Legionnaires and beast alike froze mid-stride, then dissolved into clouds of glittering, crimson-stained dust that rained silently onto the sand.
The horrific silence after the scream was deafening.
Panic choked the Legion’s rear ranks.
Shields flared weakly, useless against resonant annihilation.
The distant cloud of settling dust registered instantly—an attack vector slicing through his vulnerable rear.
Hold the front!" His roar cut through the rising chaos.
Dragonmail plates flared with sudden, searing azure light as Zaron’s spirit surged, responding to imminent threat.
Time seemed to warp; Geralt blurred forward, not running, but *flowing* impossibly fast across the dunes, sand kicking up in crystalline arcs behind him.
He passed Oreck, already reversing course with terrifying speed, the green arrows along his greaves blazing like emerald beacons pointing *back*.
Together, they closed the distance in heartbeats, arriving as a second Dragan drew breath to scream.
He *leaped*, armored form crashing onto the Dragan’s broad back like a meteor.
His gauntleted fist, wreathed in crackling temporal energy, slammed down *not* onto bone, but onto the thick cartilage ridge at the base of its skull—a critical resonator node.
The impact pulsed visibly, a ripple of distorted air.
The Dragan’s scream choked into a wet, gurgling gasp.
Its sonic blast misfired internally; blood and ruptured organs sprayed from its jaws.
His cleaver wasn’t aimed to kill, but to *disable*.
The obsidian edge, humming with chroniton green, sliced precisely through the thick tendon anchoring a third Dragan’s colossal leg to its hip.
The creature bellowed in agony, crashing sideways, its next scream lost in a roar of primal pain and frustration.
The immediate threat stalled, but the peril was far from over.
The screech of southern reinforcements echoed—allied Dregans summoned by the breach.
The southern Dregans erupted onto the scene with terrifying silence, their larger, sand-polished hides absorbing the harsh sunlight.
The lead Dragan’s territorial challenge cry wasn’t aimed at Geralt’s forces, but at their northern kin—a wave of discordant force slamming the raging attackers sideways.
The northern Dregans, consumed by genetic fury, whirled as one pack-beast, abandoning the legionnaires entirely.

Oreck’s assessment was a low growl felt in Geralt’s bones: "Territory." The ensuing clash was apocalyptic—a whirlwind of snapping spines, sonic blasts detonating prematurely, sand fused instantly into glass.
Legionnaires watched, shields trembling against debris, as giants tore each other apart.
Lyra’s bio-scanner whirred frantically, tracking the horrifying cascade of energy signatures.
The victors weren’t saviors; they were conquerors clearing their hunting grounds.
Their departure left only the groans of the dying northern Dragan Oreck crippled and the settling crimson dust of its vaporized kin.
Silence reclaimed the desert, heavier now.
"Regroup," he commanded, the word scraping raw.
"Secure the wounded." Bodies crystallized beyond the shield perimeter glittered accusingly under the merciless sun.
Ren retched violently into the sand.
"Stabilize Halvar *now*." The healer nodded, already moving, filaments pulsing urgent cyan towards the stunned veteran.
The deeper enemy waited, casting shadows far darker than Dragan packs.
The air thickened, losing its knife’s edge dryness.
Boots crunched on gravelly earth now, sand yielding to cracked hardpan radiating heat upward like coals.
Ahead, blinding white salt flats stretched—cracked crusts whispering false promises of water under the midday glare.
Geralt’s dragonmail hummed differently here; Zaron’s spirit recoiled faintly against the mineral scent carried on sudden, sluggish breezes.
Thorny bushes clawed upward from the baking soil, razor-edged grasses scratching against scaled greaves.
Silence draped itself like a shroud.
Only the scuff of weary boots and the low thrum of shield generators.
Then, a sharp cry echoed—Corporal Vess stumbled backward from a low mound.
Her boot sank calf-deep into liquefied clay where solid ground seemed moments before.
The earth pulsed visibly around her leg, drawing her deeper.
Oreck surged forward, his chroniton-enhanced strength anchoring him on firmer ground as he seized Vess’s arm.
"Don’t struggle!" Mika barked, seeing the suction intensify.
"Guide her slowly!" Geralt ordered, scanning the treacherous basin—this was no desert.
This was the land’s wounded throat.
Steps that felt solid crumbled into sucking mud without warning.
Sweat plastered hair to necks, no longer evaporating but soaking into grit-stained fatigues.
Ahead, the Breathing Pyramid rose—a scarred monument of volcanic rock and sagging sandstone, its lower half dissolving into the shimmering haze of swamp breath.
Stagnant ponds festered; alkali rims glowed poisonous white beneath twin moons.
Mosquitoes whined incessantly, a maddening chorus Lyra silenced near Halvar with targeted micro-pulses from her rig.
"Pulse… stronger here," Oreck rumbled, cleaver tip pointing downward.
Beneath their feet, the faintest tremor resonated—sub-audible, felt through bone.
Geralt halted the column before the pyramid’s shadowed entrance, a collapsed archway channeling dark water inward.
His claw traced the air before the eroded stone.
A shimmering resonance field flickered—dry volcanic stone resisting humid decay.
His armored palm pressed against the stone.
The stone groaned… shifted… revealing a slick descent into cloying darkness smelling of wet earth and ozone.
Its trapped lightning would be their guide… or their grave.
Mika tightened her grip on her shock-lance.
Watch for voids." The descent began.
Chroniton arrows on Oreck’s greaves cast jade fractals over algae-slick walls.
Silence choked the passage—not the desert’s stillness, but the swamp’s heavy, listening quiet.
Only the rhythmic drip of condensation pierced it.
Geralt moved like shadow given form, Zaron’s spirit coiled taut within the armor, sensing dimensional fractures.
A legionnaire’s boot slipped on wet stone.
Mika’s hand snapped out, steadying him.
"Scan your footing." Lyra’s filaments pulsed cyan, mapping the unstable geometry.
"Resonance spikes ahead," she whispered, voice tight.
Unstable." The corridor widened abruptly into a cavernous cistern.
At its heart, rising from black water, stood the Void Spire—a needle of pure obsidian humming with trapped thunder.
Above it, refracted through murk, the Buried Luminaire’s crystalline core glowed… but its light was sickly, threaded with veins of deep violet corruption.
Under siege." Oreck’s growl vibrated the air.
Shapes coalesced in the gloom—pale, multi-limbed, drawn by the dissonant light.
"Multiple bio-signatures… converging!" Shapes slithered from flooded alcoves—pale, segmented horrors with too many jointed limbs ending in needle-claws.
Bioluminescent spores dotted their carapaces, pulsing sickly violet in sync with the corrupted Luminaire.
They moved silently, chitin scraping wet stone.
Jorik’s arrow flew first, a chroniton-tipped streak punching through a leading drake’s eye cluster.
It detonated in a spray of ichor and temporal shrapnel, staggering two others.
Oreck met the next wave head-on.
His cleaver wasn’t a blade; it was a chroniton storm.
Green energy sheared through chitin, triggering cascading temporal decay in the wounded.
Flesh aged centuries in seconds, crumbling to dust.
Mika coordinated the shield wall—legionnaires locking overlapping fields just as a drake spat a glob of acidic phlegm.
It sizzled against the barrier, filling the air with acrid fumes.
He moved toward the Spire, Zaron’s spirit blazing within him.
The dragon-armor resonated, countering the violet corruption threading the Spire’s base.
She needs access!" Integration became combat triage.
The healer scrambled forward, rig unfolding.
Her target wasn't the drakes, but the Luminaire itself.
Stabilize the anchor… or lose them all to the Queen’s hunger.
Water rippled against Geralt's boots as he reached the Spire’s obsidian base.
Zaron’s spectral talons manifested fully now, clawing at the violet corruption like physical rot.
Each touch sent shivers through the stone, dislodging calcified sediment.
Lyra slid beside him, her rig’s injectors unfolding like metallic spiders.
"Direct infusion required!" she yelled, voice strained against the Spire’s rising thrum.
But the pattern’s chaotic!" Geralt’s helm tilted, focusing past the battle.
He heard it—the Luminaire’s fractured song beneath the Queen’s static.
Through it." Her filaments flared cyan, syncing with Geralt’s dragon-resonance… seeking harmony in dissonance.
For an instant, the Luminaire’s core shone pure, trapped lightning refracted through murk—a dazzling prism of sound made visible.
Twice the size of the others, its carapace bore scars of Anunnaki implants forcibly welded to its spine.
A beam of corrupted luminescence ripped toward Lyra—a mimicry of the Spire’s own power, twisted and vile.
The blast hammered her back, cracking her kinetic field like glass.
She skidded across wet stone, gasping.
Oreck intercepted the Alpha’s follow-up strike.
His cleaver met its descending claw.
Halvar and Torren flanked the beast, blades useless against its thick plates.
Jorik peppered its eyes, buying seconds.
Geralt’s focus never wavered from the Spire.
Azure light coiled around the obsidian needle, peeling back the violet corruption strand by agonizing strand.
Lyra’s hands trembled as her filaments fused deeper into the resonance field.
Its tail whipped, sending Torren crashing into a crumbling wall.
Halvar leapt atop its back, dagger stabbing for implant seams.
The beast bucked, flinging him into dark water.
Mika staggered upright, shock-lance spitting unstable energy.
The Alpha recoiled, its corrupted light beam sputtering.
His cleaver plunged into the beast’s neck joint.
The chroniton blade targeted the pulsing Anunnaki implant grafted to its spine.
Only the drip of water and the Luminaire’s pure, strengthening hum remained.
"Anchor stabilized… for now." The violet veins were faded ghosts.
But beneath the obsidian spire, the water still churned.
Geralt turned toward the Stair’s shadowed continuation.
Each downward step crushed Geralt’s shoulders tighter.
Condensation wept from fused basalt walls, slick beneath scaled boots.
Air thickened—metal-tanged humidity pressing like drowned lungs.
No desert wind dared trespass here.
Only the Spire’s ghost-light bled upward, painting jagged silhouettes that danced with each flicker.
The Luminaire’s buried song wasn’t heard—*felt*.
It vibrated ribcages, warping inner ears.
Shieldbearer Jax stumbled sideways, helmet amplifying the dissonance into a skull-drilling whine.
Below, the shaft breathed—a subsonic groan resonating through stone and bone alike.

Geralt’s dragonmail flared azure, Zaron’s will anchoring him against the pull. *One step lower and your stomach drops—the resonance isn’t sound, it’s gravity bending.* He gripped Corvin’s pauldron, hauling him upright against the trembling wall.
Sweat carved trails through grime on pale faces.
A cathedral-sized dome unfolded—stalactites hung like shattered chandeliers, wrapped in crystalline filaments humming with trapped resonance.
Water pooled ankle-deep, hiding razor-edged mineral ridges.
Corporal Vess’s whisper echoed back seconds later—*"Watch the—"*—overlapping her own caution.
Hallucinations whispered commands Mika never gave.
Legionnaire Ren spun, shock-lance raised toward empty darkness.
"Who’s there?" Oreck’s amber gaze scanned the vaulted ceiling.
Translucent shapes clung there—blind, choral fauna, spider-limbed and thin as paper.
Harmonic pulses rippled across their bodies.
They flowed down stalactites like liquid shadow, drawn to the sound’s epicenter.
Mika’s hand signal was sharp: *Absolute silence.* Survival demanded it.
Every scrape of boot, every rasp of breath, risked awakening the choir.
Basalt yielded to fossilized roots—massive, petrified veins from the swamp above.
Water surged without warning, thigh-high torrents roaring through twisting tunnels.
Legionnaires braced against carved walls slick with millennia of scum.
Lyra’s rig flashed methane warnings: 82% saturation.
Geralt pressed forward, Zaron’s resonance mapping safe paths through labyrinthine gloom.
Torren argued with Halvar, voice tight.
"We entered this gallery *minutes* ago!" Halvar rasped back, "Hours!
Humidity and void resonance stretched seconds into subjective eternities.
Trust Geralt’s armored back cutting through the reeking dark.
Trust Oreck’s chroniton arrows flaring green at intersections.
The obsidian Void Spire plunged downward into the Lucid Storm—an underground lake burning with captured energy, teal and blinding.
Static crackled across Geralt’s vambrace, shorting displays.
Lyra cursed as her medicae rig sparked, injectors dropping inert.
Bioluminescent horrors—eel-things woven from lightning—snaked through the water, drawn to kinetic fields.
Torren’s reflection shimmered on the lake surface—not his scarred face, but a sneering warlord draped in Anunnaki sigils.
Halvar recoiled from his own reflection: a skeletal husk bleeding shadow.
Geralt saw Zaren’s dragon form fractured, scales edged in violet rot.
Boots struck water—and the storm ignited.
Arcs of raw electricity spiderwebbed outward, seeking conduits.
Torren screamed as an eel-thing latched onto his greave, bioelectricity seizing his muscles.
Halvar hacked it free, blade sizzling.
She fired her shock-lance point-blank into the water.
Geralt waded deeper, Zaron’s spirit warring with the storm’s pull.
Azure scales flared brighter, repelling arcs.
Zaren’s dragon-shadow coiled in the ripples: *Accept her power.
Let them burn.* Truth’s weight crushed his ribs.
Each step sank him deeper into liquid light.
Gear’s failing!" Her own reflection showed her hands decayed, bones protruding—a healer’s failure made flesh.
Energy tendrils lashed, wrapping his legs.
Zaron roared within him, a sound swallowed by static.
Mika fought beside him, shieldless, lance spearing eel-things.
Torren dragged Halvar from the water, both convulsing.
Then came the voice—not sound, but thought etching bone:
Images flooded Geralt’s mind: Oreck disintegrating.
Legionnaires vaporized as raw power surged through him—dragon wings unfurling against the void.
The Luminaire’s core glowed hungrily behind tangled roots.
Beneath the water, the storm gathered strength.
The cracked sandstone stairs vanished beneath ankle-deep water slick with condensation.
Each step echoed too loud, too soon—a drumbeat swallowed by damp stone.
Geralt led, boots sinking into unseen silt.
Above, the ceiling wept mineral tears that hissed against heated armor seals.
Below, the Void Spire’s ghost-light bled upward, painting the shaft walls into jagged, shifting silhouettes.
Legionnaire Bren gasped behind him—a wet, choked sound.
The Luminaire’s buried song wasn’t heard. *Felt*.
It vibrated ribcages, warping inner ears.
Shieldbearer Kael stumbled sideways, his helmet amplifying the dissonance into a skull-drilling whine.
The shaft breathed—a subsonic groan resonating through stone and bone.

Translucent shapes clung above—blind choral fauna, spider-limbed and paper-thin.
Harmonic pulses rippled across their bodies.
A power-cell slipped from Bren’s belt. *Clang.* The creatures *stirred*.
They flowed down stalactites toward the sound.

Let them burn.* Truth’s weight crushed him.
Each step sank deeper into liquid light.
The Luminaire pulsed beneath the tangled roots—not a beacon, but a predator.
Its core glowed hungrily behind knotted metal, half-submerged in opaque teal liquid.
Voices layered—Geralt heard Mika’s clipped orders, Oreck’s tactical silence, and his own thoughts looping back as distorted commands: *Leave them.
Chroniton crystals embedded in the ceiling wept glowing droplets that hissed where they struck the water.
Legionnaire Bren clutched his helmet as his own reflection screamed silently up at him—a hollow-eyed prisoner bound in chains he’d forged.
"The roots… they’re shifting!" Lyra yelled, voice frayed.
The Luminaire’s casing trembled, metal vines uncoiling like awakened serpents.
One lashed out, wrapping Torren’s ankle, dragging him toward the luminous pool.
Halvar lunged, shock-lance spitting futile sparks against the resonant shield.
Geralt’s gauntlet vibrated—Zaron’s roar reduced to static.
The choice carved itself into his bones.
Five hundred souls vaporized as raw power surged through him—dragon wings unfurling against the void.
Beneath the water, the roots tightened.
Lyra’s medicae rig spat a final spark.
Her reflection showed bone where flesh should be—a healer’s failure made manifest.
She met Geralt’s eyes across the churning light.
An anchor." The Luminaire flared, its light searing.
Mika fought beside him, shieldless, lance spearing another root-tendril.
Chroniton droplets rained down like molten stars.
Halvar hauled Torren free, both bleeding phosphorescent fluid.
The cavern walls shimmered, dissolving into resonance.
Geralt plunged his clawed hand into the pool.
Azure light flared from his gauntlet, weaving through the metal vines.
For a heartbeat, the storm stilled.
Reflections cleared—Mika’s fierce determination, Oreck’s unwavering vigilance, Lyra’s exhausted resolve.
The pool churned black as the Luminaire’s light dimmed to ember-red.
Something deeper than roots stirred in the depths.
Revelation’s price waited in the dark.
Cover the Commander!" Legionnaires formed overlapping arcs, sparking lances pointed outward.
Lyra scrambled backward, rig spitting diagnostics.
It’s rejecting the corruption!" Her voice trembled with awe.
Droplets fell like molten lead, searing water into toxic steam.
Oreck hauled Torren onto a petrified root-island, the warrior’s leg weeping phosphorescent ichor.
Halvar stood guard, blade singing as he severed another questing tendril.
The cavern groaned—a sound of tectonic agony.
Geralt remained waist-deep, Zaron’s light fighting the encroaching shadow.
Lyra’s fingers flew over her Medicae Rig’s scorched panel.
A fragment anchored in stasis..." Her eyes locked on Geralt’s dragonmail.
"...the other became the storm." The implications hung thick.
Luminara’s light judged because it was broken.
Her harmony sought not a master, but harmony itself.
Zaren’s ghost-shadow whispered again: *Burn the roots.
But Mika’s reflection—steadfast, unyielding—answered silently: *Anchor us*.
Below Geralt’s boots, the lakebed trembled.
Wisdom came not from dragons, but desperation.
Geralt tore a chroniton arrow from Oreck’s quiver—its green glow stark against Zaron’s blue.
He plunged it into the root-mass.
Not azure or emerald, but pure, blinding white.
For an instant, Geralt saw her: Luminara, fractured yet radiant, a being of crystallized harmonics reaching through the void.
The spire’s full resonance hammered him.
Zaron roared—a sound of triumph and dissolution.
Above the dunes, Earth’s Spire flared gold, announcing their presence to the cosmos.
Geralt stood on obsidian glass fused by his own power.
Legionnaires stared, shields dark, lances lowered.
Luminara’s voice hummed through Geralt’s shattered armor: *"Anchor established.
Transit protocols initiated."* Mika touched the liquid—not teal, but silver.
"She’s mapping coordinates." Lyra collapsed, her rig humming as it repaired itself.
The null state… she didn’t hide.
She synchronized." Halvar flexed his hand—no trace of decay.
Chroniton sight showed branching paths: Mars, scarred and waiting; Dragon Nebula, shimmering beyond time.
Geralt’s gauntlet pulsed with hers—a crystalline key embedded in his palm.
"She’ll tear it open." Mika traced the fractal patterns forming on the sand.
"And announce us to every spire in the network." Legionnaires murmured—fear, awe.
Lyra injected Halvar with stabilized chroniton fluid.
The desert wind carried whispers: Anunnaki signatures converging.
Oreck slammed his cleaver into the glass.
We walk it." Geralt flexed his new hand.
Luminara’s final warning echoed: *"They hunt keepers.
They hunt me."* The dunes shimmered.
"Then we hunt first." Five hundred souls readied weapons.
The sand hardened beneath Geralt’s boots.
Silver light bled from cracks, forming a vast sigil—a dragon coiled around a spire.
Oreck planted chroniton arrows at each node.
Halvar gripped his blade, knuckles white.
Torren limped forward, ichor-stained bandage taut.
Sand fused into obsidian beneath them.
Static hummed in teeth and bone.
Mika materialized mid-lunge, lance spearing its eye.
The Dragonwayne Nebula shimmered in the black.
The Mars spire stabbed the horizon—cracked, weeping violet corruption.
Behind them, the silver gateway collapsed.
Ahead, shambling forms emerged from dust-devils.
Luminara’s light pulsed in Geralt’s palm.
"She’s weak here," Lyra warned, scanner glitching.
"Corruption resonance overwhelming." Oreck nocked an arrow.
"Then we purify." Geralt drew his sword.
Only the spire’s broken heartbeat throbbed.
Geralt felt her fragmentation—**Earth Prime Resonance Keeper**, stretched thin across dimensions.
Her whispers were static: *"Anchor points destabilizing... locus integrity failing..."* Her nature revealed: not a weapon, but a symphony.
Harmonics clashed as Mika’s lance pierced a construct’s core.
Instead of shattering, it *screamed*—a discordant note silencing her comms.
"Disrupting her harmonics!" Halvar roared, cleaving through rusted plating.
Each strike fed the spire’s corruption.
Zaron’s resonance surged—blue fire met violet decay.
Aelxion’s spectral gaze pierced the void.
The **Draconic Warden of Breach** saw the frayed connection—Geralt’s key struggling against Mars’ dissonance.
Green light wove a containment field.
Lyra injected her rig into the fused sand.
"Resonance override initiating!" Luminara’s voice strengthened: *"Syncing... anchor restored."* The spire pulsed gold.
A path opened—a fracture in the spire’s base.
The core nexus!" But Nyxthoria’s warning echoed from the nebula: Balance demanded sacrifice.
Reality rippled like heat haze over a forge.
Massive silhouettes glided across the Martian stars—not ships, but **living eclipses**.
Scales caught the light of Phobos, glittering with crimson fire and nebular gold.
A roar unheard in vacuum shook the regolith beneath Geralt’s boots.
Beside him, VALDRASIL units phased into existence.
Serpentine forms flickered between crystalline matter and emerald energy, executing impossible turns.
Their jittering movements left afterimages—ghostly shimmers clawing at the mind.
One VALDRASIL streaked toward a bronze dragon, scales catching a dying sun’s fury.
Silence screamed louder than battle cries.
Halvar’s grip loosened on his blade.
Not fire, but void made manifest.
Where they struck a VALDRASIL, the serpent didn’t explode.
Geralt’s chroniton-sight flared—Zaron’s panic spiking at the violation of physics.
Beside him, Lyra’s scanner shorted out, vomiting sparks.
Torrents of plasma—stellar fire twisted into solar prominences—erupted in electric blue and violent purple.
Metal vaporized into lingering nebulae—glowing gravesites slowly fading.
Patches of space kaleidoscoped into probability cascades.
Light bent around invisible singularities, lensing stars into impossible arcs.
Bio-electric pulses flashed—green and violet lightning arcing between combatants.
The entire sky ignited in neon auroras: corrosive yellows pulsing with distant detonations.
Below the cosmic ballet, Geralt’s army stood exposed.
Violet corruption pulsed from the spire’s base—Luminara’s fracture weeping darkness.
VALDRASIL phantoms skimmed low, targeting the Legion’s chroniton signatures.
Mika’s lance flared uselessly against phased matter.
A VALDRASIL solidified overhead, crystalline jaws wide.
Its bio-electric maw crackled—aimed at Halvar.
Dragonfire met green lightning in a silent detonation.
Shields buckled under stray entropy shrapnel.
Two men crystallized mid-sprint—their terror frozen in obsidian glass.
"Feeding the spire’s decay!" Geralt’s symbiosis with Luminara faltered.
Her light dimmed against Mars’ dissonance.
The Dragon Nebula watched—T’Zurakai’s sapphire gaze tracking every branching doom.
A serpentine shadow—longer than Vaelros’ wingspan—coiled into existence. **Void-wyrm**.
Starlit scars marred its anti-light scales.
It heard resonance—the spire’s corruption, Geralt’s key, VALDRASIL’s discord.
Dread washed cold through Geralt’s veins.
But Luminara’s agony sang too loud.
From swirling dust—a pinprick ignored by gods and wyrms alike—four figures solidified.
Youthful faces etched with ageless authority.
Recognition flared hot in Geralt’s chest—impossible recognition.
First: Clad in dragonmail like his own—but azure scales crackling with primal lightning.
He moved—a blur of cobalt and storm-fire—fist striking the void-wyrm’s descending snout.
Second: Robes of solar fusion—amber, gold, blinding white.
It curved impossibly, slicing through phased VALDRASIL constructs like they were smoke.
Each touch ignited silent supernovas within their cores.
Armored in twilight silk and starlight plate.
Her fingers danced in empty air—reweaving spacetime like thread.
VALDRASIL phantoms near Halvar simply... ceased existing.
Barely visible—a flicker at the edge of sight.
Where his passing shade touched crystalline soldiers?
They crumbled into harmless obsidian sand.
His eyes—Geralt’s own eyes—locked onto Geralt’s.
Then—a bronze dragon descended like fury incarnate.
They leapt onto its back—four impossible saviors—vanishing into the cosmic storm above.
Leaving only the echo of thunder and the scent of ozone deep within Geralt’s soul.
A fleeting pause—a breath stolen from chaos.
"Now!" Geralt roared, his voice slicing through stunned stillness.
The Mars Spire pulsed, its violet corruption recoiling from Luminara’s renewed harmonic surge within Geralt’s gauntlet.
The fracture lay exposed—a jagged tear weeping entropy.
